notes: Official releases keep their observation periods; 15 October external-debt data describes August. The October IMF figures are forecasts. QRIS user and merchant totals describe June, not current GoPay share. Dated FX, energy and equity observations are provider snapshots; incomplete sessions are excluded from comparison histories. Remaining reference indicators retain independent-review labels.
reference_notes: BI-Rate decision date is 23 Sep 2026 (per sources), not 17 Sep. Next BI meeting 21 Oct 2026; next FOMC 27-28 Oct 2026 (not verified).

BI-Rate 2025 monthly path (cuts Jan, May, Jul, Aug, Sep 2025 to 4.75%; holds Oct-Dec) is from Bank Indonesia's decision record. Sources here confirm 150bp of cuts in the cycle to Sep 2025, the Sep 2025 cut (OCBC), the Dec 2025 hold at 4.75% (FocusEconomics), and 5.75% as the 'highest since Apr 2025' (Trading Economics). The 2026 path (4.75% Jan-Apr; +50bp May to 5.25%; +50bp Jun to 5.75%) is from Kontan/Bisnis/IDN Financials.
JCI prev close (6,094) and YTD (-31.4%) are derived: prev from the -2.59% move, YTD vs the 30 Dec 2025 close of 8,646.94 (Bisnis.com). The Jan-2026 high was ~8,936 (Republika).
USD/IDR series mixes Katadata spot snapshots; the 8 Oct Katadata title (17,916.4) conflicts with the 17,887.8 prev close cited on its 9 Oct page; the latter is used.
Credit growth prev (12.67%) is Jun 2026, not Jul 2026 (Jul not found).
UST 10Y prev (5.31%) is implied from a -4bp move.

Gaps (null): e-Conomy SEA 2026 not yet published (expected ~Nov 2026), so the 2025 report is used and the 2024 GMV base is unstated; multifinance prev/yoy and NPF prev not found; Aug 2026 unemployment not yet released; QRIS value (nominal) growth and user/merchant counts not found; no CPI monthly history for 2025.

Fuel: no Pertalite change found in 2026 (Rp10,000; government says it is unchanged through end-2026). Non-subsidised prices rose (Pertamax Turbo, Dexlite from 1 Sep 2026; BI cites non-subsidised fuel increases in Sep CPI). The Pertamax pre-2026 baseline was not verified.
CPI history sources: Kontan/Fortune (Jan 3.55, Feb 4.76, Mar 3.48), BPS (Apr 2.42, May 3.08), Trading Economics (Jun 3.34, Jul 2.88, Aug 3.19), BI (Sep 3.28).
P2P Jun 2026 outstanding (Rp105.14trn, +25.88% yoy) from MetroTV; Jul (Rp105.63trn, TWP90 4.32%) from Bisnis.com.

news.title: Taiwan FTC blocks Grab’s proposed foodpanda acquisition
news.implication: Treat cross-ownership, information rights and remedies as early diligence issues in platform M&A. Taiwan’s decision is not an Indonesian merger ruling or a measured GoFood market-share gain.
news.nextAction: Check issuer responses, appeal and transaction termination status, any applicable break-fee terms, and Indonesia-specific competition analysis before changing a deal case.

news.title: Grab details merchant AI, driver waiting-location guidance and voice-enabled kitchen tools
news.implication: Useful GoFood and Gojek product benchmarks: actionable merchant advice, practical driver waiting spots and lower-friction order handling. A patent or application does not prove adoption or profit gains.
news.nextAction: Compare merchant task completion, driver idle distance and kitchen-order errors in controlled pilots; confirm local rollout and intellectual-property scope.

news.title: Grab launches ChatGPT training for Thai drivers and merchants
news.implication: Benchmark Gojek partner productivity, merchant support and AI partnerships; the Thailand rollout does not establish Indonesia adoption or lost GoTo share.
news.nextAction: Compare partner engagement, task completion and incremental support costs; test build-versus-partner options before assigning earnings uplift.

news.title: Grab schedules Q3 2026 results for 2 November
news.implication: Align the next GoTo–Grab comparison around disclosed operating and credit metrics rather than mismatched reporting periods.
news.nextAction: Update the head-to-head board after publication; keep current Q2 actuals and acquisition proposals separately labelled.

news.title: Grab Thailand and OpenAI expand partner AI training through GrabAcademy
news.implication: Pair merchant and driver AI tools with practical training, then measure workflow adoption and incremental partner earnings rather than attendance alone.
news.nextAction: Test a limited GoFood Merchant / driver cohort against a matched holdout; assess task success, repeat use, support demand, cost and partner outcomes.

news.title: Grab says foodpanda Taiwan acquisition remains under regulatory review
news.implication: Regional M&A execution and integration capacity are relevant to GoTo’s competitive scenarios. Taiwan approval risk must not be treated as a completed transaction or an Indonesian market-share change.
news.nextAction: Monitor Taiwan regulator decisions, final transaction conditions and closing; compare integration capacity with Grab’s other announced acquisitions.

news.title: Grab, SoftBank and PETROS sign Sarawak AI framework agreement
news.implication: Benchmark strategic AI partnerships and capital commitments; no Indonesia operating benefit or GoTo earnings effect is established.
news.nextAction: Watch binding commitments, ownership, capital spending and milestones before comparing build-versus-partner economics.

news.title: Grab describes a regional quality standard for 5-Star Eats
news.implication: Provides a concrete operating benchmark for linking customer signals to merchant quality and retention in GoFood. Store-level app ratings are not the restaurant-quality scores used by this programme.
news.nextAction: Compare merchant completion, fulfilment incidents, repeat orders and quality-label governance against GoFood; verify each market’s rollout.

news.title: Grab proposes $1.49bn acquisition of 60% of Atome Financial
news.implication: A scaled BNPL and cash-lending competitor could increase pressure on GoPay's distribution and underwriting. Assess product overlap and partnership alternatives before assigning a financial impact.
news.nextAction: Track regulatory approval, closing and loan performance; benchmark GoPayLater, GoPay Pinjam and Bank Jago distribution.

news.title: Grab plans to execute remaining approximately $900m buyback authority
news.implication: Adds a relevant capital-return benchmark for GoTo's board. Compare repurchase value creation with liquidity needs, financing capacity and prospective deal returns.
news.nextAction: Monitor actual repurchases and reconcile capital returns with acquisition commitments and financial-services funding.

news.title: Grab profitability improves
news.implication: Benchmark sustainable margins and incentive intensity, not headline profit.
news.nextAction: Track subsequent operating disclosures and reassess GoTo strategic implications.

cact.event: Taiwan FTC blocks Grab’s proposed foodpanda acquisition
cact.implication: Treat cross-ownership, information rights and remedies as early diligence issues in platform M&A. Taiwan’s decision is not an Indonesian merger ruling or a measured GoFood market-share gain.
cact.status: Prohibited by Taiwan FTC · not completed
cact.details: Taiwan’s FTC prohibited the combination on 21 October. It cited competition concerns including Uber’s approximately 13.1% economic stake in Grab and found the offered commitments insufficient.
cact.evidence: Original public source read; facts, dates, geography and analyst interpretation kept separate.

cact.event: Mynt / GCash completes Philippine IPO listing; PHP60.9bn gross offering
cact.implication: Benchmark wallet-based distribution and capital access for GoPay. Separate new issuer cash from shareholder sales before comparing funding capacity.
cact.details: PSE confirms Mynt listed as GCASH on 20 October. The PHP60.9bn offering combines primary and secondary shares. PSE reports 140,725 GCash subscribers invested about PHP1.1bn through the app.
cact.evidence: Original primary page read; dates and geography retained. GoTo interpretation is analyst analysis.

cact.event: Sea discusses a possible Monee IPO and plans Sea Cloud
cact.implication: Assess GoPay’s standalone capital needs, governance, shared-service costs and separation readiness. Sea Cloud is a capability-commercialisation benchmark, not evidence that GoTo should build a competing cloud.
cact.status: Management aspiration and product plan · no priced or completed IPO
cact.details: Sea’s filed 20 October staff email says Monee is approaching readiness to stand independently and that going public could provide resources. Sea also says it will offer its internally developed cloud capability as an AI-first enterprise platform.
cact.evidence: Original public source read; facts, dates, geography and analyst interpretation kept separate.

cact.event: Bluebird expands Solo fleet to 100 taxis; MyBluebird accounts for 47% of bookings
cact.implication: Compare city-level fleet density, advance booking and service reliability with GoCar; these local figures do not establish national market share.
cact.status: Original source reviewed; facts and analyst interpretation separated
cact.details: ANTARA reported that Bluebird expanded its Solo/Surakarta fleet to 100 taxis in total. The local business reported average quarterly demand growth of 17% and a 47% MyBluebird booking share.
cact.evidence: Original public source read; reporting period, programme dates and publication dates retained separately.

cact.event: Grab details merchant AI, driver waiting-location guidance and voice-enabled kitchen tools
cact.implication: Useful GoFood and Gojek product benchmarks: actionable merchant advice, practical driver waiting spots and lower-friction order handling. A patent or application does not prove adoption or profit gains.
cact.status: Issuer-described products and patent status; outcomes not independently measured
cact.details: Grab describes its Merchant AI Assistant, RideGuide Smart Destination and Cloud Printer. The assistant’s architecture has a Singapore patent; applications in Indonesia and other markets remain pending. Smart Destination is also in the patent-application process.
cact.evidence: Full official article dated 16 October reviewed; Singapore grant and pending applications distinguished.

cact.event: Akulaku reports police cooperation over alleged identity-data misuse
cact.implication: Benchmark identity verification, partner-platform controls and customer remediation across consumer-credit competitors.
cact.status: Allegations under investigation; company statement reported
cact.details: VOI reports Akulaku Finance Indonesia’s statement that it is working with Bandung and West Java police on alleged misuse of customer data by external parties on a partner platform. The investigation does not establish proven liability or a verified loss attributable to GoTo.
cact.evidence: Full publisher article reviewed; allegations and company claims remain attributed; no court or regulator finding reviewed

cact.event: Sea Labs and Google AI Futures Fund expand applied-AI collaboration
cact.implication: Raises the competitive benchmark for AI-enabled commerce and payments. Treat it as a technology collaboration, not a disclosed funding round or evidence of Indonesia revenue uplift.
cact.status: Collaboration announced; commercial results not disclosed
cact.details: Sea announced access to selected Google frontier models and technical expertise for Sea Labs. The collaboration spans its existing Garena, Shopee and Monee ecosystem and builds on the February 2026 partnership in gaming, agentic commerce and payments. No financing amount or equity investment was disclosed.
cact.evidence: Full issuer release dated 15 October 2026 reviewed.

cact.event: Grab launches ChatGPT training for Thai drivers and merchants
cact.implication: Benchmark Gojek partner productivity, merchant support and AI partnerships; the Thailand rollout does not establish Indonesia adoption or lost GoTo share.
cact.status: Announced training; adoption figures reported by management
cact.details: Grab targets over 3,000 Thai partners for training, within a regional goal above 30,000. Management reports 275,000 Thai merchants using its AI assistant and 120,000 drivers adopting its driver assistant. These are issuer-reported adoption figures, not measured profit gains.
cact.evidence: Official source reviewed; strategic implications are analyst interpretation

cact.event: Grab schedules Q3 2026 results for 2 November
cact.implication: Align the next GoTo–Grab comparison around disclosed operating and credit metrics rather than mismatched reporting periods.
cact.details: Grab’s IR overview lists a 14 October announcement scheduling Q3 results for 2 November 2026. No Q3 earnings figures are available from that announcement.
cact.evidence: Official IR indexed listing reviewed; direct retrieval restricted; exact call time not independently verified.

cact.event: Grab Thailand and OpenAI expand partner AI training through GrabAcademy
cact.implication: Pair merchant and driver AI tools with practical training, then measure workflow adoption and incremental partner earnings rather than attendance alone.
cact.details: Grab announced ChatGPT training for more than 3,000 Thai drivers, riders and restaurant operators. The release reports over 275,000 merchants using its merchant AI assistant and over 120,000 drivers using its driver assistant.
cact.evidence: Original primary page read; dates and geography retained. GoTo interpretation is analyst analysis.

cact.event: VinFast offers dealers up to US$60,000 per electric-motorcycle showroom
cact.implication: Distribution incentives could affect Electrum’s dealer access and driver-EV options. Compare vehicle financing, swap coverage and operating cost before estimating a competitive effect.
cact.status: Reported dealer program; rollout to verify
cact.details: TNGlobal reports a dealer package in Indonesia and the Philippines: up to US$40,000 base support, up to US$5,000 for opening by 31 October and up to US$15,000 for partners opening at least three stores. Eligibility and showroom standards apply.
cact.evidence: Full TNGlobal article reviewed; issuer statement described by publisher

cact.event: Superbank describes AI-assisted assessment of underserved borrowers
cact.implication: Benchmark Bank Jago and GoPay lending on risk-adjusted returns, acquisition costs and model controls. AI adoption alone is not a verified underwriting advantage.
cact.details: Asian Banking & Finance interviews Superbank CFO Melisa Hendrawati about using behavioural data and AI in credit assessment, retaining human judgment and monitoring model bias and performance. The article does not quantify a default-rate improvement.
cact.evidence: Article and publisher listing reviewed; listing date 12 October, page relative timestamp varies

cact.event: Grab says foodpanda Taiwan acquisition remains under regulatory review
cact.implication: Regional M&A execution and integration capacity are relevant to GoTo’s competitive scenarios. Taiwan approval risk must not be treated as a completed transaction or an Indonesian market-share change.
cact.details: Grab’s 12 October statement says its proposed foodpanda Taiwan acquisition is still being reviewed and it has not formally entered the market. The company describes commitments to delivery partners and merchants, and Taiwan-specific data-governance arrangements. These are the acquirer’s representations, not regulatory clearance.
cact.evidence: Full official source reviewed; geographical scope and announced versus completed status retained.

cact.event: Grab, SoftBank and PETROS sign Sarawak AI framework agreement
cact.implication: Benchmark strategic AI partnerships and capital commitments; no Indonesia operating benefit or GoTo earnings effect is established.
cact.status: Framework signed · exploration and roadmap pending
cact.details: The parties signed an agreement to explore AI and digital infrastructure in Sarawak, Malaysia, and develop a phased roadmap. The release does not disclose an investment amount or a completed deployment.
cact.evidence: Official joint release reviewed; forward-looking scope preserved.

cact.event: ShopeePay Malaysia expands Zurich partnership into life insurance
cact.implication: Use this Malaysian wallet cross-sell as a partnership benchmark for GoPay. Indonesia availability, licensing and economics are not established by the Malaysian launch.
cact.details: Zurich Life Insurance Malaysia announced distribution through ShopeePay and a two-year savings-and-protection plan starting at RM500. It builds on existing general-insurance partnerships; lower future entry premiums and family takaful are plans, not current launches.
cact.evidence: Official partner release reviewed; geographical scope retained

cact.event: OVO runs a third round of its illegal-gambling reporting programme
cact.implication: Examine customer reporting, fraud triage and response quality as trust features for GoPay; rewards alone do not establish reduced fraud.
cact.status: Official programme terms reviewed; publication date not stated
cact.details: OVO’s official campaign page describes a third round running 1 October–30 November 2026. The reporting and reward programme has eligibility rules including an active OVO Nabung by Superbank account and a minimum six-month account tenure.
cact.evidence: Original public source read; reporting period, programme dates and publication dates retained separately.

cact.event: Grab describes a regional quality standard for 5-Star Eats
cact.implication: Provides a concrete operating benchmark for linking customer signals to merchant quality and retention in GoFood. Store-level app ratings are not the restaurant-quality scores used by this programme.
cact.status: Regional quality framework described; market-specific execution
cact.details: Grab describes aligning its food-quality labels around a regional baseline, with local standards. Ratings, written feedback and fulfilment reliability inform merchant recognition; Malaysia’s tourism guide and other market programmes retain their local scope.
cact.evidence: Full official source reviewed; geographical scope and announced versus completed status retained.

cact.event: MyBluebird links first-transaction missions to loyalty rewards
cact.implication: Test whether a reward earned on a first trip generates a profitable second trip rather than subsidising already-active riders.
cact.details: Accounts registered from 1 July to 30 September 2026 without a prior transaction could earn a Rp5,000 later-trip code by completing their first transaction during 1–31 October.
cact.evidence: Original Bluebird page reviewed on 19 October 2026; event and reporting dates retained.

cact.event: Grab plans to execute remaining approximately $900m buyback authority
cact.implication: Adds a relevant capital-return benchmark for GoTo's board. Compare repurchase value creation with liquidity needs, financing capacity and prospective deal returns.
cact.details: Grab intends to use remaining share-repurchase authority over the next 12 months, funded from existing cash. Execution depends on market conditions; the full amount is not guaranteed.

cact.event: Grab proposes $1.49bn acquisition of 60% of Atome Financial
cact.implication: A scaled BNPL and cash-lending competitor could increase pressure on GoPay's distribution and underwriting. Assess product overlap and partnership alternatives before assigning a financial impact.
cact.details: Grab signed for a controlling 60% stake, including $260m of primary capital. Closing is expected by Q3 2027, subject to approvals; it is not completed.

cact.event: Grab to deploy remaining ~$900M of buyback authorisation within 12 months
cact.details: Grab intends to use the remaining ~$900M of authorised repurchases over the next 12 months, taking cumulative buybacks since 2024 to ~$1.75B (>10% of Class A shares at current price); funded from $5.4B net cash liquidity (30 Jun 2026).
cact.implication: Signals Grab sees its own equity as cheap while still holding ample firepower for M&A; sets a capital-return benchmark GoTo investors will compare against GoTo's own buyback cadence.

cact.event: inDrive expands beyond ride-hailing into food, groceries, ads and fintech
cact.details: inDrive is putting most new investment into food and grocery delivery, scaling 'Ride Media' ads (25 markets, >2,000 advertisers/month) and inDrive.money (driver loans in LatAm +118% YoY in H1 2026); hired ex-Delivery Hero exec to lead food.
cact.implication: A low-cost ride-hailing challenger building a super-app playbook raises medium-term pressure on Gojek's GoFood and ads monetisation in price-sensitive segments.

cact.event: Akulaku confidentially files for Hong Kong IPO of up to US$500M
cact.details: Ant Group-backed Akulaku filed confidentially for a HK listing seeking US$300-500M; it was reportedly valued at ~US$2B in 2025 and had earlier considered a US listing.
cact.implication: A listed BNPL/digital-bank rival gains capital and a public valuation mark that will be read across to GoTo Financial (GoPayLater, Bank Jago); also signals HK as a viable venue for Indonesian fintech.

cact.event: Sea Q2 2026: revenue +48% to US$7.8B, Shopee GMV US$38.3B
cact.details: Revenue US$7.8B (+48.1%), net income US$458M, adj. EBITDA US$917M; Shopee GMV +28.4% to US$38.3B; Monee loan book US$11.1B (+62.5%, NPL90+ 1.0%); Garena bookings US$763.5M. CEO targets ~US$1B Shopee FY adj. EBITDA.
cact.implication: Shopee is out-growing the market while turning profitable, keeping pressure on Tokopedia (where GoTo retains an economic interest) and showing Monee scaling credit faster than GoTo Financial.

cact.event: Sea repurchases US$416.8M of shares in Q2 2026
cact.details: Under its US$1.0B programme, Sea bought back 4.7M shares for US$416.8M in Q2 2026; Garena deferred-revenue effect to be excluded from adj. EBITDA from Q3 2026.
cact.implication: Sea is now returning capital at scale, putting ASEAN internet peers (including GoTo) in a capital-return valuation framework.

cact.event: Uber Q2: scale, cash flow and investment gains require separate readings
cact.implication: Use as a global operating and capital-allocation benchmark; it is not a direct Indonesian mobility share measure.
cact.details: Uber reports $14.191bn revenue and $2.819bn adjusted EBITDA. GAAP net income includes a $1.6bn pre-tax equity-investment revaluation benefit.
cact.evidence: Primary source reviewed · Source publication date

cact.event: DoorDash Q2: delivery growth, membership and acquisition effects
cact.implication: A global delivery and merchant-software benchmark for GoFood, not an Indonesian competitive-share estimate.
cact.details: DoorDash reports 970m orders, $33.078bn Marketplace GOV and $914m adjusted EBITDA. Order growth excluding Deliveroo was 17%, versus 27% reported.
cact.evidence: Primary source reviewed · Source publication date

cact.event: Alfamind coaches agent-led virtual-store selling through local networks
cact.implication: Test whether local agents add incremental profitable demand beyond consumer-app acquisition.
cact.status: Official operating guide reviewed; unit economics not disclosed
cact.details: An August Alfamind guide describes virtual-store selling through personal networks and WhatsApp, supported by coaching. The existing operating model is not a new 2026 launch.
cact.evidence: Official Indonesian operating guide reviewed; English summary edited on 19 October 2026.

cact.event: Grab Q2 2026: record results, FY2026 guidance raised
cact.details: Revenue US$997M (+22%), adj. EBITDA US$168M (+54%, 16.9% margin), profit US$235M incl. US$307M Superbank remeasurement gain; FY2026 guidance raised to revenue US$4.10-4.15B and adj. EBITDA US$720-740M (from US$4.04-4.10B / US$700-720M).
cact.implication: Grab's widening margin and scale gap vs GoTo strengthens its position in any merger negotiation and its relative valuation.

cact.event: Grab authorises new US$750M share repurchase
cact.details: New US$750M authorisation brings cumulative buybacks to US$1.75B since 2024; the US$250M ASR and US$101M contingent forward purchase under the Feb 2026 programme were completed in July 2026.
cact.implication: Reinforces Grab's excess-cash position; a reference point for GoTo's capital allocation narrative.

cact.event: Blibli H1 2026: revenue +55%, net loss cut 43%
cact.details: Revenue Rp14.83T (+54.6% YoY); net loss attributable narrowed 43% to ~Rp708bn from Rp1.26T in H1 2025.
cact.implication: Djarum-backed Blibli is closing the profitability gap in e-commerce, raising the floor for Indonesian e-commerce competition and comps.

cact.event: 8% ride-hailing commission cap in effect from 1 July 2026
cact.details: Government confirmed app commissions capped at 8% (drivers keep 92%), down from up to 20%, effective 1 July 2026; implementing Perpres still being finalised across ministries.
cact.implication: Directly compresses Gojek and Grab two-wheeler take rates; levels the field with low-commission players (Maxim, inDrive) and reshapes the economics of a GoTo-Grab combination.

cact.event: Bank Jago H1 2026 net profit +49% to Rp189bn
cact.details: Net profit Rp189bn (+49%), loans Rp26.6T (+24%), gross NPL 0.8%, 20.1M customers; AGM approved no FY2025 dividend and board changes; partners incl. Bibit, Stockbit, BFI Finance.
cact.implication: GoTo's banking affiliate is scaling profitably, supporting GoTo Financial's lending and the value of GoTo's stake.

cact.event: Courting Express (TAXI) fleet after GoTo contract ends
cact.details: TAXI ended its GoTo fleet contract on 2 Jul 2026 and is exploring Green SM.
cact.implication: GoCar loses fleet supply; check other GoCar fleet partners for churn.

cact.event: Indonesian e-motorcycle launch and 2027 CKD plan at Subang
cact.details: Three models at Rp17.5-22m with battery subscription; V-Green 2,000+ swap points in Java; talks with ride-hailing operators.
cact.implication: Threat to Electrum and to GoTo control of the driver EV transition; also a possible fleet partner. Decide partner-or-compete before Grab does.

cact.event: Bluebird launches Prime with hybrid and electric fleets
cact.implication: Test demand for a clearly defined premium ride tier, balancing willingness to pay against fleet and driver costs.
cact.details: Bluebird announced Prime using Toyota Innova Zenix Hybrid and BYD E6 vehicles, with launch availability in Jakarta and BYD E6 service in Bandung, Surabaya, Medan and Bali.
cact.evidence: Original Bluebird page reviewed on 19 October 2026; event and reporting dates retained.

cact.event: Tokopedia trims e-commerce workforce again, following Shopee and Lazada
cact.details: Tokopedia (TikTok-controlled) cut more e-commerce staff after two rounds of layoffs the previous year; Shopee and Lazada also made cuts.
cact.implication: Continued consolidation of Tokopedia into TikTok Shop reduces GoTo's influence over the asset; a talent pool and cost-discipline benchmark.

cact.event: New e-commerce rules: 0.5% PPh 22 withholding, seller NIB, fee transparency
cact.details: From 1 Jul 2026 platforms withhold 0.5% tax on merchant turnover (PMK 37/2025); Permendag 19/2026 requires seller NIB, fee disclosure, anti-predatory pricing, local-product priority and import floor prices.
cact.implication: Raises compliance costs and may slow seller growth for Shopee and TikTok Shop/Tokopedia; reduces cross-border price pressure.

cact.event: Maxim cuts app commission to flat 8% from 1 July 2026
cact.details: Maxim Bike commission moved to a flat 8% (from 8-15%, ~12% average) under Perpres 27/2026; Maxim says rider fares will not rise.
cact.implication: Removes Maxim's commission-based driver recruitment edge; competition shifts to fares and incentives.

cact.event: Grab and Gojek adopt 8% two-wheeler commission under Perpres 27/2026
cact.details: Grab Indonesia (GrabBike) and Gojek (GoRide) to apply 8% commission from 1 July 2026, down from a 20% cap; President Prabowo announced Perpres 27/2026 on May Day 2026.
cact.implication: Hits Gojek and GrabBike revenue per trip equally; key input to Indonesian mobility forecasts and merger synergy cases.

cact.event: Bluebird shareholders approve Rp166 per-share dividend
cact.implication: Consider the balance between fleet investment, cash generation and shareholder distributions when comparing capital intensity.
cact.details: The AGM approved Rp166 per share from FY2025 earnings. The release scheduled payment for 10 July 2026; payment completion is not verified by this announcement.
cact.evidence: Original Bluebird page reviewed on 19 October 2026; event and reporting dates retained.

cact.event: Kredivo's Krom Bank passes 1M accounts, Rp10T deposits
cact.details: Krom Bank (BBSI), controlled by Kredivo, passed 1M accounts and Rp10T deposits; Q1 2026 net profit Rp70.2bn (+98.6%) but impairment charges more than doubled to Rp455bn.
cact.implication: Kredivo is building a deposit-funded balance sheet to compete with GoPayLater/Bank Jago; rising impairments are a credit-cycle watchpoint.

cact.event: Grab takes control of Superbank, consolidates it
cact.details: Singtel transfers its Superbank shares to GXS Bank, lifting Grab's combined direct and indirect stake above 50%; Superbank consolidated into Grab Financial Services from May 2026.
cact.implication: Grab now controls a listed Indonesian digital bank, a direct rival to GoTo Financial and Bank Jago in deposits and lending.

cact.event: Sea Q1 2026: revenue +47% to US$7.1B, first US$1B adj. EBITDA quarter
cact.details: Revenue US$7.1B (+46.6%), net income US$438M, adj. EBITDA ~US$1B; Shopee GMV US$37.3B (+30.2%) but Shopee adj. EBITDA fell to US$223M on reinvestment; Monee revenue US$1.2B (+57.8%).
cact.implication: Shopee is reinvesting margin to take share, which means more promo intensity in Indonesian e-commerce.

cact.event: Krom Bank loans nearly double to Rp9.88T in Q1 2026
cact.details: Loans grew 98% YoY to Rp9.88T, with Kredivo and KrediFazz as main channelling partners; channelling is Krom's core 2026 lending strategy.
cact.implication: Faster-scaling bank-plus-BNPL model competes directly with GoTo Financial's consumer lending.

cact.event: Bluebird Q1 revenue rises 11.6%; MyBluebird users grow 22.4%
cact.implication: Compare service reliability and fixed-price adoption with GoCar repeat usage; this release does not establish market share.
cact.details: For Q1 2026, Bluebird reported Rp1.45tn revenue, Rp341.8bn EBITDA and Rp157bn net profit. MyBluebird users increased 22.4% and fixed-price usage 29.2% year on year.
cact.evidence: Original Bluebird page reviewed on 19 October 2026; event and reporting dates retained.

cact.event: Grab Q1 2026: revenue +24%, guidance reaffirmed
cact.details: Revenue US$955M (+24%), adj. EBITDA US$154M (+46%, 16.2% margin), profit US$120M; reaffirmed FY2026 guidance of US$4.04-4.10B revenue and US$700-720M adj. EBITDA.
cact.implication: Steady execution keeps Grab's valuation premium over GoTo intact.

cact.event: Blibli proposes non-preemptive issue of up to 9.5bn shares
cact.details: Up to 9.5bn new shares (6.92% of capital): 4.5bn for MESOP and 5bn for capital raising; EGM on 4 Jun 2026.
cact.implication: Fresh equity gives Blibli more competitive runway in e-commerce and retail.

cact.event: Grab launches US$250M ASR and up to US$150M contingent forward purchase
cact.details: US$250M accelerated share repurchase with JPMorgan (~54.9M shares initial delivery) and up to US$150M CFP with Morgan Stanley, under the US$500M Feb 2026 programme.
cact.implication: Aggressive buyback execution signals management sees undervaluation; it also reduces Grab's share count ahead of any stock-funded deal.

cact.event: Grab to acquire foodpanda Taiwan from Delivery Hero for US$600M
cact.details: US$600M cash, cash-free and debt-free; closing expected H2 2026, with migration to the Grab app by early 2027. Grab's first expansion outside Southeast Asia.
cact.implication: Shows Grab's appetite for large food-delivery M&A beyond ASEAN; reduces cash for, but does not preclude, an Indonesia deal.

cact.event: Grab signs $600m foodpanda Taiwan acquisition agreement
cact.implication: A geographic expansion and execution benchmark; Taiwan is not an Indonesian market-share observation.
cact.status: Signed; completion not independently established in this update
cact.details: Grab announced a cash-free, debt-free acquisition agreement, subject to approvals, with closing expected in H2 2026.
cact.evidence: Primary source reviewed · Source publication date

cact.event: Bukalapak FY2025 swings to Rp3.14T profit on investment gains
cact.details: Net profit Rp3.14T vs Rp1.54T loss in 2024; revenue Rp6.51T; net investment income of Rp2.37T was the main driver.
cact.implication: Bukalapak is now effectively a cash-rich investment vehicle with virtual-goods operations; a possible consolidation or acquisition target rather than a marketplace rival.

cact.event: Sea FY2025 net income more than triples to US$1.6B
cact.details: FY2025 revenue +36.3% to US$22.9B and net income ~US$1.6B.
cact.implication: Sea's profitability at scale widens the gap with GoTo and Tokopedia in e-commerce and fintech.

cact.event: DANA eyes IDX IPO, awaiting market timing
cact.details: DANA (Espay Debit Indonesia Koe) says an IPO is part of its long-term strategy and is studying the BUKA and GOTO IPOs; backers include Sinar Mas and Lazada, with Ant International as tech partner.
cact.implication: A listed DANA would give a public valuation peer for GoPay and could fund more aggressive wallet competition.

cact.event: Emtek unit buys 4.36% more of Bukalapak for Rp674bn
cact.details: Emtek subsidiary PT Kreatif Media Karya bought ~4.49bn BUKA shares (~4.36%) on 19-20 Feb 2026 for Rp674.3bn at Rp150, citing investment purposes.
cact.implication: Emtek creeping up its stake points to tighter control or a possible take-private; Emtek is also a key Superbank shareholder.

cact.event: Grab to acquire US investing app Stash at US$425M EV
cact.details: Grab is buying 100% of Stash Financial (EV US$425M): 50.1% at closing in cash and stock, the rest over three years. Stash has >US$5B AUM and >1M paying subscribers, with >US$60M adj. EBITDA expected in 2028. Closed July 2026.
cact.implication: Grab is expanding fintech internationally and using stock as currency; it shows Grab will pay for wealth and investing capabilities that GoTo has only through partners (Bibit, Stockbit).

cact.event: Grab FY2025: first full-year net profit; US$500M buyback
cact.details: FY2025 revenue US$3.37B (+20%), adj. EBITDA US$500M, net profit US$200M, adj. FCF US$290M; board authorised a US$500M buyback; targets US$1.5B adj. EBITDA by 2028.
cact.implication: Grab's 2028 target and its first full-year profit set a high bar for GoTo's profitability narrative.

cact.event: Grab entity raises direct Superbank stake to 11.10%
cact.details: A5-DB Holdings (Grab) bought 362.7M SUPA shares for IDR382.08bn (avg IDR1,053) on 14-19 Jan 2026, lifting its stake from 10.03% to 11.10%.
cact.implication: An early step in Grab's creep to control of Superbank, completed in May 2026.

cact.event: Superbank (SUPA) lists on IDX after ~US$167M IPO, oversubscribed ~318x
cact.details: IPO priced at Rp635/share; demand was ~318.7x oversubscribed with >1M orders; shares jumped 24.4% (limit-up) on debut.
cact.implication: Gives the Grab/Emtek/Singtel-backed digital bank a public currency and valuation mark against Bank Jago (ARTO); strong retail demand shows investor appetite for digital banks.

cact.event: Subang, West Java EV plant opens
cact.details: First Indonesian assembly plant; supports local-content (TKDN) rules for EV incentives.
cact.implication: Lower local price points for EVs that could be offered to GoRide and GoCar drivers.

cact.event: GoTo CEO Walujo to step down; seen as lifting Grab merger prospects
cact.details: DealStreetAsia reported Patrick Walujo would step down as GoTo CEO, with Patuwo likely to take over, after SoftBank, Peak XV and others reportedly sought the change.
cact.implication: A leadership change aligned with major shareholders could clear the way for a Grab combination; critical for corp-dev scenario planning.

cact.event: Sea announces up to US$1B share repurchase programme
cact.details: Board authorised repurchase of up to US$1B of ADSs, with timing depending on market conditions.
cact.implication: Sea's first major buyback in this cycle marks a shift to capital return and a rerating comparator for ASEAN tech.

cact.event: Indonesia reportedly backs GoTo-Grab merger; Danantara eyes golden share
cact.details: Reuters reported the government now fully backs a possible GoTo-Grab merger after initial opposition, with Danantara in talks for a golden share; the combined entity would hold >91% share (Euromonitor). Antitrust and driver-income conditions remain.
cact.implication: The most material strategic event for GoTo: a state-sanctioned path to combination with a likely golden-share veto and driver-welfare conditions.

cact.event: Grab Q3 2025 results; FY2025 guidance raised
cact.details: Revenue US$873M (+22%), adj. EBITDA US$136M (+51%); FY2025 guidance lifted to revenue up to US$3.4B and adj. EBITDA up to US$500M.
cact.implication: Continued upgrades strengthen Grab's hand and its relative valuation ahead of merger talks.

cact.event: Bukalapak launches further buyback of up to Rp420.79bn
cact.details: Up to Rp420.79bn from internal cash, running 24 Oct 2025 to 23 Jan 2026; the remainder of an earlier Rp1.13T programme.
cact.implication: Bukalapak keeps returning cash rather than reinvesting in commerce, confirming its retreat as an operating competitor.

cact.event: Grab makes equity investment in robotaxi firm May Mobility
cact.details: Grab took an undisclosed 'significant' stake in May Mobility to integrate its AVs into Grab's fleet, matching and routing systems, with Southeast Asia deployment from 2026.
cact.implication: Grab is building an autonomous-mobility moat; GoTo has no comparable AV partnerships.

cact.event: Tokopedia lays off 420 in second 2025 round
cact.details: 420 employees cut, bringing total layoffs since the January 2024 TikTok Shop merger to ~1,070.
cact.implication: Deepening integration under TikTok; GoTo's residual stake is increasingly passive.

cact.event: Grab commits strategic equity investment in WeRide
cact.details: Grab committed to an equity investment in WeRide (NASDAQ: WRD) to deploy L4 robotaxis and shuttles in Southeast Asia; completion expected by H1 2026.
cact.implication: Same as May Mobility: Grab is pulling ahead on the AV and long-term cost-structure narrative.

cact.event: Bukalapak extends buyback with Rp1.13T budget
cact.details: Bukalapak set aside up to Rp1.13T for a continued share buyback period (Jul-Oct 2025).
cact.implication: Large capital return from a cash-rich former rival; lowers BUKA float ahead of possible further Emtek consolidation.

cact.event: Grab prices upsized US$1.5B zero-coupon convertible notes due 2030
cact.details: Upsized from US$1.25B; 0% coupon, conversion price ~US$6.55 (40% premium); proceeds for general corporate purposes, strategic flexibility including acquisitions, and a concurrent ~US$273.5M buyback.
cact.implication: Explicitly builds an M&A war chest at the height of GoTo merger speculation.

cact.event: Grab reportedly targets GoTo acquisition at ~US$7B valuation
cact.details: Reports said Grab had hired advisers and held financing talks for a deal valuing GoTo at ~US$7B, with GoTo keeping Indonesian financial services; GoTo said no decision had been made.
cact.implication: Sets the reference valuation and structure (fintech carve-out) for any GoTo-Grab transaction.

cact.event: Emtek subsidiary buys 9.73bn Bukalapak shares
cact.details: An Emtek subsidiary acquired 9.73bn BUKA shares, increasing the group's control of Bukalapak.
cact.implication: Emtek consolidation of BUKA; potential precursor to a take-private or asset reshuffle.

cact.event: Bukalapak exits physical-goods marketplace, pivots to virtual products
cact.details: Bukalapak announced it would close physical-goods marketplace selling and focus on virtual products (top-ups, bills) and its Mitra network.
cact.implication: Removes a marketplace competitor; Bukalapak's sellers and buyers migrate to Shopee, TikTok Shop/Tokopedia and Blibli.

research.title: BI: August external debt reaches US$459.3bn; private debt declines
research.summary: Bank Indonesia reports external debt of US$459.3bn, up 5.6% year on year. Private debt is US$195.6bn, down 0.8%; total external debt equals 30.9% of GDP. The release is dated 15 October and measures August.
research.relevance: Adds context for currency, offshore financing and refinancing scenarios; it is not GoTo debt or a company-specific funding signal.
takeaways: Public and private borrowing can move differently. Currency and maturity exposure matter alongside aggregate debt.
Compare FX liabilities, hedge coverage and refinancing maturities for any transaction or portfolio exposure; keep issuer liabilities separate.
research.evidence: Official source reviewed; strategic implications are analyst interpretation

research.title: Akulaku reports police cooperation over alleged identity-data misuse
research.summary: VOI reports Akulaku Finance Indonesia’s statement that it is working with Bandung and West Java police on alleged misuse of customer data by external parties on a partner platform. The investigation does not establish proven liability or a verified loss attributable to GoTo.
research.relevance: Benchmark identity verification, partner-platform controls and customer remediation across consumer-credit competitors.
takeaways: Identity misuse can affect fraud losses, complaints and trust. An allegation is not a regulator finding or proof of system-wide credit deterioration.
Monitor police or regulator findings, remediation and incident scope; compare authentication and complaint controls without assuming cross-platform contagion.
research.evidence: Full publisher article reviewed; allegations and company claims remain attributed; no court or regulator finding reviewed

research.title: Indonesia classification consultation: implications for funding scenarios

takeaways: Track consultation milestones; do not book hypothetical outflows.

research.title: GoTo October EGM: approvals confirmed by official minutes
research.summary: The October 14 meeting approved cancellation of 32,186,417,803 Series A treasury shares, with resulting issued and paid-up capital of 1,158,958,579,417 shares. Catherine Hindra Sutjahyo’s resignation became effective at the meeting’s close.
research.relevance: Primary evidence now replaces the earlier press report. Treasury cancellation is not a new cash buyback; reconcile legal implementation and remaining treasury shares before changing the model denominator.

Treasury cancellation is not new cash repurchase expenditure.
October voting details and legal-effective share count remain to be reconciled.

research.title: Grab launches ChatGPT training for Thai drivers and merchants
research.summary: Grab targets over 3,000 Thai partners for training, within a regional goal above 30,000. Management reports 275,000 Thai merchants using its AI assistant and 120,000 drivers adopting its driver assistant. These are issuer-reported adoption figures, not measured profit gains.
research.relevance: Benchmark Gojek partner productivity, merchant support and AI partnerships; the Thailand rollout does not establish Indonesia adoption or lost GoTo share.
takeaways: Training and in-app tools may improve partner workflows. Retention, service quality and support costs determine commercial value.
Compare partner engagement, task completion and incremental support costs; test build-versus-partner options before assigning earnings uplift.
research.evidence: Official source reviewed; strategic implications are analyst interpretation

research.title: IMF October briefing: global growth forecast at 3.1% for 2026 and 3.4% for 2027
research.summary: The IMF briefing describes energy pressure, uneven AI-led demand and limited fiscal room as key risks. Its 2026 and 2027 growth numbers are forecasts. The media release is dated 14 October and describes a 13 October briefing.
research.relevance: Stress-test consumer demand, funding costs and driver energy costs alongside company-level data. Global forecasts do not quantify Indonesian platform growth.
takeaways: Energy shocks can weaken purchasing power while raising costs; concentrated technology investment can support growth unevenly.
Use separate demand, fuel-cost and discount-rate scenarios; wait for source-verified country tables before changing Indonesia forecasts.
research.evidence: Official source reviewed; strategic implications are analyst interpretation

research.title: QRIS: zero MDR now covers all merchant categories for transactions up to Rp100,000
research.summary: BI’s updated table confirms the 1 October expansion. Micro merchants retain 0% up to Rp500,000 and 0.3% above; other regular merchants pay 0% up to Rp100,000 and 0.7% above. The 17 August issuer-of-policy release and 13 October table agree.
research.relevance: Reconcile GoPay and Midtrans merchant ticket mix and net fee sharing. Growing low-ticket transactions may not produce proportional fee revenue; the full MDR is not GoTo revenue.
takeaways: The fee threshold changes merchant economics and payment fee pools. Higher adoption may offset some pressure, but the net earnings effect needs transaction-level data.
Update merchant-category and ticket-size assumptions; compare monetization with DANA, OVO, ShopeePay and acquiring partners.

research.title: BPJPH confirms Wajib Halal starts 18 October; special provisions still being prepared

It says special provisions for certain UMK and imported products are being prepared, and supervision will use guidance rather than sweeping operations. Product scope and exceptions need the applicable implementing rules.

Special provisions are still being prepared; do not treat them as finalized exemptions.
Review the applicable product scope rather than assuming every merchant must be removed.

research.title: Sarawak AI framework: partnership scope and execution questions

Assess capital allocation, governance and product adoption before assigning value.

research.title: September 2026 adjusted base money: growth and liquidity-incentive basis
research.summary: Bank Indonesia reports adjusted M0 of Rp2,353.1tn, growing 9.3% year on year versus 16.3% in August. The adjusted series accounts for liquidity-incentive effects; it is not M2.
research.relevance: Adds a liquidity signal for bank funding and credit scenarios. Base money alone does not establish GoPay demand or Bank Jago deposit growth.
takeaways: Year-on-year growth moderated; the money stock did not necessarily decline.
Adjusted M0 and broad money M2 are different series.
Assess liquidity together with bank funding and credit data.

research.title: ASEAN+3 Regional Economic Outlook - October 2026 Update

research.title: ASEAN+3 Financial Stability Report 2026

Cyber risk, leverage and concentrated AI valuations warrant monitoring.

research.title: WEO October 2026 Chapter 3: corporate tax and cross-border spillovers
research.summary: The IMF finds that tax differences affect investment location and profit allocation, while anti-avoidance rules increasingly align profits with real activity. The effects of tax cuts depend on how governments finance them.
research.relevance: Analyst application: assess tax substance, transfer pricing, intellectual-property ownership and after-tax cash flows when structuring cross-border investments. This chapter does not establish a change to Indonesian law.
takeaways: Headline statutory rates do not capture the full effective tax burden.
Investment location, profit allocation and financing have different tax and economic channels.
Model after-tax returns and obtain jurisdiction-specific tax advice before preferring a holding structure.
research.evidence: October issue; publication day not established for this chapter. PDF opening analysis pp. 1–3 and tax-mechanism discussion p. 5 reviewed; not a full WEO forecast review.

research.title: Asian Development Outlook September 2026
research.summary: The outlook assesses growth amid prolonged energy disruption and El Niño, with developing Asia-Pacific growth forecasts of 5.0% for 2026 and 5.1% for 2027.
takeaways: Forecasts differ by economy.
Energy, food and tighter financial conditions are downside channels.

research.title: GoTo October 2026 EGM invitation and proposed capital reduction
research.summary: The September invitation proposed cancelling 32,186,417,803 Series A treasury shares and approving Catherine Hindra Sutjahyo’s resignation. The meeting has since been held; ANTARA reports approval of both agendas on 14 October.

Shareholders subsequently reported to approve both agendas on 14 October.

Distribution and access to customers are prominent strategic motives.
Wealth and asset management gained activity within the regional sample.

takeaways: Net distributions turned positive after three years of outflows.
Fundraising reached a 12-year low; deal multiples rose to 13.4x.
AI disruption and operational value creation require deeper diligence.
research.evidence: Reviewed primary PDF — Overview and at-a-glance sections of actual PDF

research.title: Global Private Equity Report 2026
research.summary: Bain describes a narrow global buyout recovery driven by megadeals, with liquidity and fundraising still constrained.
research.relevance: Prioritize proprietary sourcing and operational synergies; consider corporate buyers and liquidity-driven sellers, with careful scope comparisons.
takeaways: 2025 buyout deal value rose 44% to US$904bn; exit value rose 47% to US$717bn.
Overall deal count declined 6%; 13 megadeals generated most value growth.
Distributions stayed below 15% of NAV for four years.
research.evidence: Reviewed primary PDF — Actual PDF pages 3–8 overview

research.title: GoTo Investment History and Governance Explainer
research.summary: The issuer explains funding history, historical shareholder roles and 2021 Tokopedia and DKAB restructuring transactions.
takeaways: Shareholder participation and a technology supplier relationship are different.
Historical restructuring is not a current capitalization table.
research.relevance: Use to clarify holding routes and due-diligence questions, alongside primary filings.
research.evidence: Issuer narrative reviewed; this is a company statement rather than an independent legal determination.

research.title: Global M&A industry trends: 2026 outlook
research.summary: PwC describes an uneven recovery concentrated in large transactions and well-capitalized buyers, with AI investment shaping strategic capability demand. Broader mid-market activity still faces valuation and execution constraints.
takeaways: Megadeals can lift value while volumes remain weak.
AI can motivate capability purchases and absorb investment budgets.
Operational value creation matters when financing and valuation gaps constrain deals.
research.relevance: Compare build-versus-buy cases and cash requirements for GoTo's AI and fintech capabilities. A global megadeal recovery does not establish local asset pricing.
research.evidence: Primary webpage reviewed: overview, market concentration and strategic implications.

research.title: Payment-industry reform: capability and risk requirements
research.summary: PBI 10/2025 and PADG 32/2025 introduce the payment-industry framework, including TIKMI: transactions, interconnection, competency, risk management and IT infrastructure.
research.relevance: Payments acquisitions and partnerships need a capability and integration assessment alongside revenue synergies; cyber resilience and infrastructure can require investment.
takeaways: Assess the target’s authorization, connectivity, risk controls and technology against the relevant category.
research.evidence: Official policy announcement and implementation-guide introduction reviewed. Effective date: 2026-03-31.

research.title: BNPL licensing and customer protection
research.summary: POJK 32/2025 permits BNPL through commercial banks and financing companies. Financing companies require prior OJK approval. Disclosure, data protection, collections and reporting are covered.
research.relevance: Validate the actual lending entity, authorization and partner responsibilities when screening a BNPL investment or distribution agreement.
takeaways: Map product → licensed lender → approval and consumer-disclosure obligations.
research.evidence: Official regulatory announcement reviewed; legal application depends on the lending entity. Effective date: 2025-12-15.

research.title: M&A notification: control, Indonesia nexus and timing
research.summary: PerKPPU 3/2023 requires qualifying transactions to be notified within 30 working days after legal effectiveness. It considers thresholds, control changes, affiliation and Indonesian assets or sales. A minority stake can confer control.
research.relevance: Include notification analysis and the legal-effective date in the deal timetable; minority structure alone does not resolve competition review.
takeaways: Have counsel assess the criteria using group structure and Indonesian assets / sales before signing.
research.evidence: Regulation Articles 1–3 and 6–10 reviewed; transaction-specific legal assessment remains required. Effective date: 2023-03-31.

ca.event: GoTo official EGMS minutes confirm treasury-cancellation plan and board resignation approval
ca.details: Official minutes approve cancellation of 32,186,417,803 Series A treasury shares, which would reduce issued and paid-up capital to 1,158,958,579,417 shares. Catherine Hindra Sutjahyo’s resignation took effect at meeting close. Directors were authorised to complete the capital-reduction formalities.
ca.status: Shareholder approval completed; capital implementation formalities to reconcile
ca.evidence: Bilingual official minutes pp. 1, 4–7; dated 14 October 2026.
ca.implication: Replaces secondary reporting with the issuer’s resolution. Approval does not establish completion of every legal capital-reduction step. Treasury cancellation is not a new cash buyback.

ca.event: GOTO falls 10% to Rp27; largest traded value on IDX; foreign net buy ~Rp134bn
ca.details: Close Rp27 (-10.0%); value Rp773bn, 28.1bn shares. IHSG -2.59% to 5,936. Foreign investors net bought ~Rp133-134bn of GOTO while net selling the market. Stock -46% in a month.

ca.event: Assessment: was the Sep-Oct 2026 drop caused by Morgan Stanley OTC buying of ESOP shares? - No evidence
ca.details: (1) No source identifies the sellers to Morgan Stanley; none mentions employees/ESOP/GoTo Peopleverse Fund. Timing (21 Aug-2 Sep, around MSCI exit, Rp152bn net foreign negotiated-market selling at avg IDR 24 on 1 Sep, BlackRock stake down) points to passive index funds exiting. (2) No new ESOP supply: GoTo cancelled the treasury-to-MESOP plan (Jul 2026); only recent ESOP sale found is Deputy CEO 516m at ~IDR 52 in Mar 2026; the "IDR 2" figure is the 2022 exercise price. (3) Main driver: removal of the IDR 50 floor on 28 Sep released pent-up selling; regular price fell 50->43->37->32->28 (25 Sep-1 Oct; auto-reject lower 29 Sep) and converged to the IDR 23-27 negotiated-market level. The OTC trades revealed the clearing price rather than caused the fall. (4) Morgan Stanley outright sales since 23 Sep (~1.4bn shares) are small vs daily volume; 7.4bn on 4 Sep was a repo. Gaps: IDX negotiated-market counterparties and KSEI data not obtained; two Morgan Stanley stake series (~7% vs ~5.4%) do not reconcile.

ca.event: Morgan Stanley sells 344.9m GOTO; stake 5.36% -> 5.33%
ca.details: Price not stated. A further ~70m-share sale was also reported (IDN Financials, date not captured). Combined outright sales since 23 Sep ~1.4bn shares vs ~13bn GOTO shares traded on 9 Oct alone.

ca.event: GoTo letter to IDX explains share-price volatility as technical
ca.details: Management attributes the fall to: FTSE exit (22 Jun), IDR 50 floor suppressing volume since May, MSCI exit (31 Aug) forcing passive selling that could not clear on the regular market, and the IDR 1 floor (28 Sep) letting queued sellers sell. Says it knows only of trades disclosed on IDX, is unaware of any majority-shareholder transactions (largest holder ~7%), and that the ESOP/MSOP plan for treasury shares was cancelled in favour of capital reduction. "Current share price does not reflect strengthening fundamentals."

ca.event: IDX lowers minimum price from IDR 50 to IDR 1; GOTO trades below IDR 50
ca.details: New IDX rule (applies to Special Monitoring Board/full call auction stocks per source; applicability path to GOTO not verified) effective ~28/29 Sep 2026 (source date inconsistent). GOTO traded ~IDR 37 on 28/29 Sep; Telkomsel's stake (1.99%, cost IDR 270/sh) down ~86%. GOTO top foreign net sell in early Oct 2026.

ca.event: Morgan Stanley sells 503.6m GOTO (disclosure); stake 5.40% -> 5.36%
ca.details: Per IDX >5% holder report dated 25 Sep; trade date and price not stated. Part of the ~5.4% reporting series (see 11 Sep FLAG).

ca.event: Morgan Stanley sells 450m GOTO at IDR 27
ca.details: Stake 7.0233% -> 6.9842% (80.8bn -> ~80.4bn shares). Executed before the IDR 1 minimum price took effect (28 Sep).

ca.event: Morgan Stanley buys 400m GOTO at IDR 27
ca.details: ~Rp10.8bn; stake 6.9951% -> 7.0299%. Disclosure lists Morgan Stanley & Co International Plc in an organised group with Morgan Stanley & Co LLC - Client Account. Purpose: investment.

ca.event: Morgan Stanley sells 1.39bn at IDR 29, buys 420m at IDR 28
ca.details: Net ~973m shares sold. Stake 7.059% -> 6.9745% (81.28bn -> 80.30bn shares). FLAG: IDN Financials reports a separate 997.9m sale on 11 Sep leaving 5.42% - a parallel ~5.4% series likely reflects a different Morgan Stanley reporting entity/account (filings do not reconcile).

ca.event: Morgan Stanley repo of 7.4bn GOTO shares at IDR 25-27 (not an outright sale)
ca.details: Repurchase agreement in negotiated market: 1.45bn at IDR 27 + 5.95bn at IDR 25 (~Rp187bn). Reported stake 7.38% -> 6.99%. Widely headlined as a sale, but Kiwoom (Liza Camelia Suryanata) notes it is a repo, holding is indirect/non-controlling and may include client/custodial positions; IDR 25 reflects bilateral pricing/collateral haircut, not a regular-market reference.

ca.event: Morgan Stanley buys ~21.9bn GOTO at IDR 25 (negotiated market); stake to 7.59%
ca.details: Three trades on 2 Sep: 12.57bn, ~200m and 9.22bn shares at IDR 25 (~Rp542-548bn), a 50% discount to the IDR 50 floor. Stake 5.71% -> 7.59% (87.48bn shares). Disclosed 7 Sep. Stated purpose: investment, "not aimed at control". Seller not disclosed.

ca.event: MSCI exit effective: GOTO largest net foreign sell, mostly in negotiated market at avg IDR 24
ca.details: First trading day after MSCI removal. Net foreign sell Rp152.5bn across all markets, of which Rp152.3bn in the negotiated market at an average IDR 24/share (Stockbit data). Kontan reports BlackRock stake fell sharply while Vanguard accumulated (figures paywalled). Consistent with passive index funds exiting via block trades because the regular market was pinned at IDR 50.

ca.event: Deputy President Director Catherine Hindra Sutjahyo resigns
ca.details: Resignation letter received 28 Aug 2026 (personal/family reasons); subject to EGM approval on 14 Oct 2026. No successor named.

ca.event: Morgan Stanley buys ~3.8bn GOTO at IDR 23 in negotiated market; crosses 5%
ca.details: Morgan Stanley & Co International Plc bought 3.13bn shares at IDR 23 plus ~657m via crossing (Rp87.3bn total), 54% below the IDR 50 regular-market floor. Stake 4.82% -> 5.15% (55.57bn -> 59.36bn shares). Stated purpose: investment. Ahead of MSCI Global Standard exit (effective 31 Aug). Seller not disclosed; no mention of employees/ESOP.

ca.event: MSCI removes GOTO from MSCI Indonesia (Global Standard) index, effective after close 31 Aug 2026
ca.details: Removal driven by illiquidity at IDR 50 floor; weight reduced to zero ahead of deadline. GOTO ~4% of MSCI Indonesia at end-July; estimated passive outflow ~IDR 1tn (Mirae). GoTo called it 'purely technical'.

ca.event: Management calls a reverse stock split 'one possible option'; still evaluating
ca.details: On the Q2 2026 call, management called a reverse split 'one possible option' to address the share price but said it is not straightforward in Indonesia, has few precedents and is viewed negatively by the public. Options are still being evaluated. Bisnis (31 Jul 2026) reported GoTo weighing the risks of a reverse split to lift the stock from the IDR 50 floor. No proposal, ratio or EGM agenda found. The 14 Oct 2026 EGM agenda covers only the capital reduction and the director resignation.

ca.event: GoTo cancels treasury-to-MESOP plan; to pursue capital reduction instead
ca.details: Dropped plan to transfer ~32.19bn treasury shares (2024-25 buyback) to the employee/management stock ownership program approved June 2025; will instead cancel them via capital reduction (~2.7% of shares). Reviewing options for a further 7.59bn treasury shares bought 19 Jun 2025 - 18 Jun 2026.

ca.event: Bank Jago and BFI Finance deny merger rumour
ca.details: Reports of a Bank Jago (GoTo/GoPay associate, ~22% per Wikipedia) and BFI Finance merger; both denied, Bank Jago said no merger in its 2026 business plan. GoTo management on Q2 call said a merger was 'still not 100% certain'.

ca.event: 8% commission cap takes effect for 2-wheel ride-hailing; GoTo cuts ODS guidance, raises fintech
ca.details: GoTo applies the 8% platform commission (from ~20%) to 2W mobility from 1 Jul 2026 under Perpres 27/2026. FY26 adj. EBITDA guidance: ODS cut to Rp1.4-1.5tn (from 1.7-1.8tn), fintech raised to Rp1.7-1.8tn (from 1.4-1.5tn), group held at Rp3.2-3.4tn. BRIDS estimates 2W = ~10% of ODS gross revenue; UOB KH cut ODS revenue by ~3%.
sources: BRI Danareksa Sekuritas, GOTO company update, 3 Jul 2026 (client-provided PDF)
UOB Kay Hian, Asian Gems Corporate Highlights, 28 Sep 2026 (client-provided PDF)

ca.details: Proposed 11 May 2026 (cash IDR 22.7tn at Mar 2026; treasury ~3.3% at Apr 2026). Agus D.W. Martowardojo reappointed President Commissioner; Marjorie Tiu Lao (Independent) and Santoso Kartono reappointed; no BoD/BoC changes. ca.details: Per IDNFinancials first hit IDR 50 on 5 May 2026 (TechTimes says closed at floor 13 May; FLAG). Stock illiquid at floor with large sell queues through Sept 2026.

ca.event: Presidential Regulation (Perpres) No. 27/2026 caps 2-wheel ride-hailing (GoRide) commission at 8%
ca.details: Announced/signed by President Prabowo on May Day 2026 (per Pluang); GOTO fell ~5-7% on 4 May. GoTo and Grab agreed (22 Jun) to cut GoRide/GrabBike commission to 8% from 1 Jul 2026. Bisnis reports formal release by State Secretariat on 8 Oct 2026, covering ride, food and goods delivery; derivative regs due Dec 2026. FLAG: signing vs. publication date inconsistent across sources. GoTo cut FY2026 on-demand EBITDA guidance by IDR 0.3tn.

ca.event: GoTo reports first-ever quarterly net profit (Q1 2026: IDR 257.9bn)
ca.details: FY2025 had record revenue but IDR 1.18tn net loss (reported 13 Mar 2026). H1 2026 net profit IDR 607.48bn on revenue IDR 10.99tn (+28.4% YoY).

ca.event: Executives exercise ESOP shares
ca.details: Hans Patuwo exercised 188.18m ESOP shares (holding 763.01m); Deputy CEO Catherine Hindra Sutjahyo acquired 515.89m via ESOP and sold all on 16-17 Mar 2026 at ~IDR 52. Program administered via GoTo Peopleverse Fund. Exercise price not disclosed.

ca.event: Bloomberg: Grab-GoTo deal hits snag over Telkomsel's ~2% stake
ca.details: Telkomsel (state-linked; ~2% of GoTo, ~US$450m invested 2020-21) reportedly unwilling to sell near market price due to state-loss liability concerns; separate buyout structure for Telkomsel being discussed. GoTo mkt cap ~US$4.2bn vs Grab ~US$18.5bn; prior >US$7bn / ~IDR 100/share all-stock idea outdated after ~30% share drop. Draft ride-hailing decree (commission cap, insurance) also unresolved. Negotiations ongoing; no conclusion. This is the LATEST substantive public reporting on deal negotiations found (as of 2026-10-10).

ca.event: EGM appoints Hans Patuwo as President Director & Group CEO, replacing Patrick Walujo
ca.details: Nominated 24 Nov 2025. Patuwo (ex-COO) replaced Walujo (~2.5-year tenure). Co-founder Andre Soelistyo and Santoso Kartono appointed commissioners, replacing Pablo Malay and Winato Kartono; director Ade Mulyana resigned. GoTo stated the EGM was not related to any corporate action plan.

ca.event: KPPU chair warns it could cancel a GoTo-Grab merger
ca.details: KPPU Chair M. Fanshurullah Asa said the merger must comply with competition law and KPPU would not hesitate to cancel it if anti-competitive; warned GoTo, Grab and Danantara against bypassing KPPU.

ca.event: SoftBank, Provident, Peak XV push to replace CEO Patrick Walujo
ca.details: Bloomberg-reported: major backers pressing for CEO change, seen as smoothing path to Grab deal (Walujo had opposed a Grab takeover).

ca.event: Government signals support for Grab-GoTo combination; Danantara golden share discussed
ca.details: Palace spokesperson said government discussed a possible merger/acquisition (~7 Nov). Reuters (13 Nov) reported government now fully supports a deal after earlier opposition; Danantara in talks to take a 'golden share' (veto rights) in combined entity; Anthony Tan met President Prabowo. State Secretary Prasetyo Hadi linked the talks to drafting of the ride-hailing Presidential Regulation. GoTo (10-11 Nov) said no decision/agreement with Grab or Danantara. Danantara CIO Pandu Sjahrir: decision rests with companies.

ca.event: IDR 4.65tn (~US$280m) 4-year term loan from DBS Indonesia and UOB
ca.details: Mandated lead arrangers PT Bank DBS Indonesia and UOB. Proceeds partly to refinance Nov 2022 facility (IDR 467bn outstanding at Jun 2025); remainder for general corporate purposes incl. investments and working capital.

ca.details: Sources said talks had ended once again.

ca.event: AGM/EGM approves new US$200m (~IDR 3.3tn) buyback (19 Jun 2025 - 18 Jun 2026), treasury-to-MESOP transfer and board changes
ca.details: Proposed 13 May 2025. Approved buyback up to US$200m (~IDR 3.3tn), max 10% of capital, on/off exchange, funded by internal cash. Approved transfer of treasury shares (from 2024-25 buyback) to employee/management stock ownership program (later reversed, see 2026-07-28). Catherine Hindra Sutjahyo became Deputy CEO/Vice President Director replacing Thomas Husted; new directors incl. Monica Lynn Mulyanto (CPO), R.A. Koesoemohadiani (Legal/Corp Sec), Ade Mulyana, Wuzhen (William) Xiong (CTO), Sudhanshu Raheja (President, GoTo Financial). Execution: 7.59bn shares repurchased 19 Jun 2025 - 18 Jun 2026 (value not found - GAP).
